revolution.title: China’s Yellow Turban Rebellion
revolution.line: After floods and poor harvests, peasants rose against a Han court run by corrupt eunuchs, and the revolt fatally weakened the dynasty.

revolution.title: Europe’s revolutions of 1848
revolution.line: After blight and failed harvests sent food prices soaring, Paris toppled a monarchy where under 1% could vote, and revolt swept Europe.

revolution.title: Sri Lanka’s protests oust the Rajapaksas
revolution.line: With food and fuel scarce and inflation over 50%, protesters stormed the president’s house, ending the Rajapaksa family’s hold on power.

railway.title: Fulton’s steamboat starts passenger service
railway.line: Robert Fulton’s steamboat began scheduled trips between New York and Albany, becoming the first steamboat service to make money.

railway.title: London opens the first underground railway
railway.line: Steam trains began carrying passengers through tunnels under London, and 38,000 people rode the Metropolitan Railway on its first day.

railway.title: Japan’s bullet train opens
railway.line: The Tokaido Shinkansen opened between Tokyo and Osaka days before the Olympics, the first railway built to run regularly above 200 km/h.

carrington.title: The great solar storm of 1872
carrington.line: A storm rivaling Carrington’s lit auroras as far south as Bombay and disrupted telegraph lines, including the Bombay to Aden undersea cable.

carrington.title: A solar storm jams US radar
carrington.line: A solar storm jammed US missile-warning radars, and commanders who suspected Soviet jamming readied aircraft until forecasters blamed the sun.

carrington.title: A solar storm downs Starlink satellites
carrington.line: A minor geomagnetic storm swelled the upper atmosphere, dragging 38 of 49 newly launched Starlink satellites down to burn up.

scramble.title: Portugal and the Ottomans clash in Ethiopia
scramble.line: Portugal sent musketeers to aid Ethiopia while the Ottomans armed the rival Adal sultanate, as both empires vied for the Red Sea.

scramble.title: Napoleon invades Egypt
scramble.line: France seized Egypt to threaten Britain’s route to India, but Nelson sank its fleet and British and Ottoman troops forced it out.

ellis.title: Vietnam’s boat people are turned away
ellis.line: As hundreds of thousands fled Vietnam by sea, neighboring states pushed boats back and declared they would accept no more.

ellis.title: California passes Proposition 187
ellis.line: After years of heavy immigration, California voters approved barring undocumented immigrants from public schools and services, though courts blocked the law.

ellis.title: South Africa’s 2008 anti-migrant riots
ellis.line: As millions fled Zimbabwe’s economic collapse for South Africa, mobs attacked foreign migrants in its townships, killing at least 62.

sykes.title: Turkish nationalists overturn the Treaty of Sèvres
sykes.line: The victorious Allies carved up Anatolia at Sèvres, but Mustafa Kemal’s nationalists fought on and won new borders at Lausanne in 1923.

sykes.title: Tuareg rebels declare Azawad
sykes.line: Tuareg rebels declared northern Mali independent as Azawad, saying France had joined it to Mali without consent in 1960.

tariffs.title: The Franco-Italian tariff war
tariffs.line: Italy raised tariffs to protect its industry, France struck back with punitive duties, and trade between them halved for a decade.

tariffs.title: Bush’s steel tariffs meet EU threats
tariffs.line: The US put tariffs of up to 30% on steel, the EU threatened $2.2 billion in retaliation, and Bush lifted them.

martians.title: The Cardiff Giant
martians.line: A “petrified man” dug up on a New York farm drew paying crowds, but it was a planted gypsum statue.

martians.title: The Piltdown Man forgery
martians.line: Fossils hailed as a missing link fooled experts for 41 years until tests showed a human skull paired with an orangutan jaw.

martians.title: The Loch Ness “surgeon’s photo”
martians.line: The Daily Mail’s photo of the Loch Ness Monster was believed for about 60 years, but it showed a toy submarine.

suez.title: Italy’s war entry closes the Mediterranean
suez.line: After Italy entered the war, most Allied shipping to the Middle East was diverted around the Cape of Good Hope until 1943.

oil.title: The 1967 Arab oil embargo
oil.line: After the Six-Day War, Arab producers cut oil to the US, Britain and West Germany, but extra US output blunted the embargo.

oil.title: Iran closes the Strait of Hormuz
oil.line: In retaliation for US and Israeli strikes, Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of world oil passes.

tiananmen.title: Beijing’s Democracy Wall movement
tiananmen.line: Crowds read posters on a Beijing wall calling democracy the “Fifth Modernization,” until a 1979 crackdown jailed Wei Jingsheng for 15 years.

tiananmen.title: Half a million march in Hong Kong
tiananmen.line: About 500,000 people marched against a national security bill they feared would curb free speech, and the government shelved it.

y2k.title: The Morris worm hits the early internet
y2k.line: A student’s program copied itself far faster than intended, jamming thousands of computers and forcing networks to disconnect for days.

y2k.title: The ILOVEYOU email worm
y2k.line: A fake love letter spread by email worldwide, infecting tens of millions of PCs and forcing many organizations to shut email down.

y2k.title: An FAA computer failure grounds US flights
y2k.line: A contractor’s deleted files crashed the FAA’s pilot-alert system, prompting the first nationwide ground stop since 9/11 and delaying over 10,000 flights.
